subject: Stack-level p95/p99 qualification & demo scheduling
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Andres Ramos <andres.ramos@lumenixlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Stack-level p95/p99 qualification & demo scheduling

Hi Andres —

Thanks again for the deep-dive earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan: 

Summary from call:
- Primary SLOs: p95 <= 220ms end-to-end, p99 <= 480ms for the Lumenix production traffic profile (95% text generation, 5% embeddings).
- Current provider reported p95 ~ 260ms and p99 ~ 720ms under burst traffic; your team is seeing tail at peak concurrency.
- Streaming footprint: client uses partial-response streaming for long-turn summaries (avg 600 tokens).

What we need from you to qualify hosted fit: 
1) Representative traffic shape (concurrent connections, average RPS, request size distribution).
2) Target concurrency during peak and acceptable warmup behavior.
3) Any regional constraints (we heard US-west + EU).

Our immediate plan:
- Send a traffic-profile CSV and an initial SLO matrix (attached). Ben will own the synthetic-run plan and data-shaping.
- Schedule a 60-min technical demo + synthetic traffic run next week to exercise streaming + KV prefetch.

Proposed demo slots (PST): Tue 9/7 10:00, Wed 9/8 14:00, Thu 9/9 08:00. Pick one and we’ll send calendar invite with .ics and drive artifacts.

Attachments: traffic_profile.csv (CSV, 12KB); slo_matrix.xlsx (Excel, 28KB)

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

—
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0143
From: Andres Ramos <andres.ramos@lumenixlabs.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stack-level p95/p99 qualification & demo scheduling

Sean —

Appreciate the summary. Confirming a couple of clarifications so Ben can design the synthetic traffic: 
- Typical sustained RPS during business hours (US-west): 180 req/s; peak bursts up to ~750 req/s for ~30s.
- 80% of calls are short (<=120 tokens); 15% mid (120-600); ~5% long streaming sessions (~600-1500 tokens).
- Concurrency target: we need p95 <= 220ms at sustained 500 concurrent sessions and p99 <= 480ms at the same concurrency with bursts tolerated up to 750 concurrent.

Region: Primary in us-west; fallback eu-west. APAC is not part of scope in this phase.

We can do Wed 9/8 14:00 PST for the demo. Please include networking details (TLS termination, whether we can simulate on our side) and any required IP allowlist. Also, what telemetry will you surface during the run? We want per-route latency, per-model KV hit-rate, and token breakdowns.

I’ll loop procurement if we need a short-term eval agreement for extended runs.

—
Andres Ramos
Head of Infrastructure, Lumenix Labs
andres.ramos@lumenixlabs.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Andres Ramos <andres.ramos@lumenixlabs.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-01T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stack-level p95/p99 qualification & demo scheduling

Thanks Andres — slot confirmed for Wed 2027-09-08 14:00 PST (60 mins). I’ll run point on synthetic traffic and the acceptance probe. Quick notes on what we’ll execute and what we need from Lumenix: 

What Redwood will run during the demo:
- Three phased passes: baseline low-load (150 RPS), sustained target (180–500 RPS), and burst window (simulate 750 RPS for 30s).
- Streaming mode: we’ll use a 5% long-turn stream profile and validate partial-chunk latency and stream commit times.
- Telemetry dashboard: we'll share a live Redwood Console link with per-route p50/p95/p99, KV cache hit-rate, per-token time, and GPU utilization.
- Failure-mode test: simulate a model-variant fallback to observe routing and cold-start tail behavior.

What we need from Lumenix:
- The traffic_profile.csv (schema: timestamp,rps,avg_tokens,concurrency) — if you can drop a sanitized sample into the Drive link we can mirror it.
- Any allowlisted IPs/ASN for the synthetic run (we can also accept traffic from your agents if you prefer to push).
- Confirm whether you need encrypted headers preserved for streaming (we can do TLS passthrough if required).

I attached a simple traffic CSV sample so you can see the columns.

Attachments: demo-traffic-sample.csv (CSV, 6KB)

—
Ben Carter
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Andres Ramos <andres.ramos@lumenixlabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Lumenix Labs (procurement) <procurement@lumenixlabs.com>
Date: 2027-09-02T02:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stack-level p95/p99 qualification & demo scheduling

On Wed, Sep 1, 2027 at 12:30 PM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Andres — slot confirmed for Wed 2027-09-08 14:00 PST (60 mins). I’ll run point on synthetic traffic and the acceptance probe.
> 
> What we need from Lumenix: the traffic_profile.csv ...

All good — I uploaded an anonymized sample to your Drive link (https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/sales/LX-4781/p95p99-slo-doc). The file contains 48 hours of production capture, with concurrent-session markers. We intentionally included a 30s spike at the 36-hour mark to show burst behavior.

Procurement: we’ll have a short eval addendum signed before the run; procurement@lumenixlabs.com will coordinate. For the APAC question: we won’t need APAC for phase 1, but can revisit in Q4.

One ask: can Redwood run the KV-prefetch + prefix-caching probe in a separate pass so we can observe cache-warm versus cache-cold p99? That metric is critical for our acceptance criteria.

—
Andres
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Stack-level p95/p99 qualification & demo scheduling

Thanks — good progress. Short action list from Redwood: 

- Ben: prepare synthetic-run script (3 phases) + separate KV-prefetch pass (due 2027-09-06).
- Laura: generate acceptance checklist (SLO gates, per-route artifacts, fallback behavior).
- Sean: send calendar invite + .ics and enable live Console view for Lumenix.

Andres — we’ll include a KV-cold vs warm pass; that will cover the p99 cache-sensitive window you described. Expect the demo invite in the next hour.

Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/sales/LX-4781/p95p99-slo-doc
